    Summarise Performance of a Prediction Model

    predsum.Rd

    Standardised reporting of binary prediction model performance. Returns a data frame of metrics (point estimate + confidence interval) and optionally renders it via reportRmd::outTable().

    predsum(
  true,
  predicted,
  cutoff = NULL,
  positive = NULL,
  ci = c("clopper-pearson", "bootstrap"),
  ci_width = 0.95,
  ci_separate = FALSE,
  nboot = 2000,
  seed = 1,
  digits = 2,
  output = "epi",
  tableOnly = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    true

    Vector of true class labels. Must be 0/1 or a two-level factor.

    predicted

    Vector of predicted values, either dichotomous (0/1) or numeric scores. If scores, cutoff must be supplied.

    cutoff

    Numeric cut-off applied as predicted >= cutoff to define the positive class. Required when predicted is non-binary and ignored (with a message) otherwise.

    positive

    The value of true treated as the positive class. Defaults to 1 when true is 0/1, or to the second level when true is a factor.

    ci

    Confidence interval method: "clopper-pearson" (default; Delong is used for AUC) or "bootstrap" (percentile).

    ci_width

    Nominal coverage, default 0.95.

    ci_separate

    logical. If FALSE (default) estimate and CI are combined in a single Value (95%CI) column. If TRUE, the output has four columns: Statistic, Estimate, lower, upper.

    nboot

    Number of bootstrap replicates, default 2000.

    seed

    integer seed set for the duration of the bootstrap so that confidence intervals are reproducible; the calling session's random state is restored afterwards. Defaults to 1. Set to NULL to leave the random state untouched, in which case intervals will vary between calls.

    digits

    Number of digits for rounding, default 2.

    output

    One of "epi" (default), "data-science", "all", or a character vector of statistic names. Recognised names (case-insensitive): prevalence, sensitivity, specificity, ppv, npv, accuracy, auc, aucpr, f1, brier, tp, fp, tn, fn, n, events, positive, cutoff. The aliases recall and precision are accepted and, when supplied, are reflected in the row labels. Preset names cannot be combined with individual statistics.

    tableOnly

    logical. If TRUE the data frame is returned silently; if FALSE (default) the data frame is rendered via reportRmd::outTable() and returned invisibly.

    Value

    A data frame of performance statistics.

    Details

    Clopper-Pearson intervals are used for proportion-based metrics (prevalence, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, accuracy). AUC uses the Delong variance estimator on the logit scale. Brier score, F1 and AUC-PR have no closed-form interval and are obtained by percentile bootstrap; when ci = "clopper-pearson" this is done automatically and a message is emitted.

    When predicted is dichotomous, AUC, AUC-PR, Brier and the cut-off row are omitted.

    References

    Delong ER, Delong DM, Clarke-Pearson DL (1988). Comparing the areas under two or more correlated receiver operating characteristic curves: a nonparametric approach. Biometrics 44(3):837-845.

    Clopper CJ, Pearson ES (1934). The use of confidence or fiducial limits illustrated in the case of the binomial. Biometrika 26(4):404-413.

    Examples

    # Simulate true labels and model scores
set.seed(1)
n <- 300
true  <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.3)
score <- plogis(rnorm(n, mean = ifelse(true == 1, 0.9, -0.9)))

# Epidemiology-style summary from probability scores
predsum(true, score, cutoff = 0.5, tableOnly = TRUE)
#> Bootstrapping CIs for Brier, F1 and AUC-PR (2000 replicates, seed = 1).
#>            Statistic     Value (95%CI)
#> 1         Prevalence 0.28 (0.23, 0.33)
#> 2        Sensitivity 0.86 (0.76, 0.92)
#> 3        Specificity 0.80 (0.74, 0.85)
#> 4                PPV 0.62 (0.52, 0.71)
#> 5                NPV 0.94 (0.89, 0.97)
#> 6           Accuracy 0.81 (0.76, 0.86)
#> 7                AUC 0.89 (0.84, 0.93)
#> 8        Sample Size               300
#> 9             Events                83
#> 10 Positive Category                 1
#> 11           Cut-off               0.5

# Data-science style (Recall, Precision, F1, Brier, AUC-PR)
predsum(true, score, cutoff = 0.5,
        output = "data-science", tableOnly = TRUE)
#> Bootstrapping CIs for Brier, F1 and AUC-PR (2000 replicates, seed = 1).
#>            Statistic     Value (95%CI)
#> 1         Prevalence 0.28 (0.23, 0.33)
#> 2             Recall 0.86 (0.76, 0.92)
#> 3        Specificity 0.80 (0.74, 0.85)
#> 4          Precision 0.62 (0.52, 0.71)
#> 5                NPV 0.94 (0.89, 0.97)
#> 6           Accuracy 0.81 (0.76, 0.86)
#> 7             AUC-PR 0.80 (0.71, 0.87)
#> 8                 F1 0.72 (0.64, 0.78)
#> 9              Brier 0.14 (0.13, 0.16)
#> 10       Sample Size               300
#> 11            Events                83
#> 12 Positive Category                 1
#> 13           Cut-off               0.5

# Custom selection with separate CI columns
predsum(true, score, cutoff = 0.5,
        output = c("sensitivity", "specificity", "auc"),
        ci_separate = TRUE, tableOnly = TRUE)
#> Bootstrapping CIs for Brier, F1 and AUC-PR (2000 replicates, seed = 1).
#>     Statistic Estimate lower upper
#> 1 Sensitivity     0.86  0.76  0.92
#> 2 Specificity     0.80  0.74  0.85
#> 3         AUC     0.89  0.84  0.93

# Dichotomous predictions: AUC, AUC-PR, Brier and cut-off are omitted
pred_class <- as.integer(score >= 0.5)
predsum(true, pred_class, tableOnly = TRUE)
#> Bootstrapping CIs for Brier, F1 and AUC-PR (2000 replicates, seed = 1).
#>           Statistic     Value (95%CI)
#> 1        Prevalence 0.28 (0.23, 0.33)
#> 2       Sensitivity 0.86 (0.76, 0.92)
#> 3       Specificity 0.80 (0.74, 0.85)
#> 4               PPV 0.62 (0.52, 0.71)
#> 5               NPV 0.94 (0.89, 0.97)
#> 6          Accuracy 0.81 (0.76, 0.86)
#> 7       Sample Size               300
#> 8            Events                83
#> 9 Positive Category                 1
